• The implementation of this was announced by former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• Article 45 was replaced as ***“The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.”***
 
• Article 51A states that **“who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.”**

questions.question: In which of the following network topologies do the connected components make a closed loop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ring topology**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ring network topology**

 
 
• The **physical and logical configuration **of a network's nodes and links is known as its **network topology**.
 
• Devices like **switches, routers, and software** with switch and router functionality are typically included in nodes.
 
• A **graph** is a common way to represent network topologies.
 
• When two computers are joined to **create a ring**, the topology is known as a **ring topology**.
 
• The nodes are linked together in a **closed-loop manner** in the ring network topology. T
 
• The message passing is **circular and unidirectional**.
 
• **Dual Ring Topology **is another way to make it bidirectional by adding two connections between each Network Node.
 
• This topology primarily utilises a **token-based system**, and each token moves in a single direction in a loop.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If a token is available in a ring topology, **the node can take it, attach the data, and the destination address, and then leave the token for communication**.
 
• The data is taken out by the receiver when this token reaches the destination node, freeing it up to carry the subsequent data.
 
• The most common type of ring network is a **metro network**, which is based on Synchronous Optical Network technology.
 
• Network topologies explain how **networks are set up and where traffic flows are located in relation to one another**.
 
• The** diagrams **can be used by administrators t**o decide where each node should be located and the best path for traffic flow**.

• It served as the **Chalukyas' capital**.

questions.question:
Complete the sentence using the options given below.

The short-run marginal cost curve is 'U'-shaped due to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the law of variable proportions.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The short-run marginal cost curve is U-shaped in the short-run **due to the operation of the "law of variable proportions".**
 
• According to the law,** the MC curve initially slopes downward till it reaches its minimum point and thereafter, it starts rising.**
 
• Therefore, it leads to a U-shape of the curve when presented graphically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A marginal cost curve is a curve that graphically represents the relation between the marginal cost incurred by a firm in the short-run product of a good or service and the quantity of output produced.
 
• This curve is constructed to capture the relation between marginal cost and the level of output, holding other variables like technology and resource prices constant.
 
• Three related curves are the average total cost curve, average variable cost curve, and average fixed cost curve.

questions.question: A certain sum at compound interest amounts to Rs. 3,025 in 2 years and to Rs. 3,327.5 in 3 years, interest compounded annually. The sum and the rate of interest p.a. are, respectively:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **compound interest**, the interest for the 3rd year is the interest on the amount at the end of the 2ⁿd year.

**Rate of Interest (R)** = [(Amount in 3 years − Amount in 2 years) / Amount in 2 years] × 100

R = [(3327.5 − 3025) / 3025] × 100 = (302.5 / 3025) × 100 = **10%**

**Sum (P)** = Amount / (1 + R/100)ⁿ = 3025 / (1.1)² = 3025 / 1.21 = **₹2,500**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,500 and 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 2 years (A₂) = **Rs. 3,025**

Amount after 3 years (A₃) = **Rs. 3,327.5**

Time period (n) = 2 and 3 years respectively.

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0654b663bdbaf72c164f8e425a02ca54dcb0ce65c30dcc818aac3c1cf0e1c07b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest for the 3rd year = A₃ − A₂

⇒ Interest = 3327.5 − 3025 = **Rs. 302.5**

⇒ Rate of interest (r) = (Interest / Principal for that year) × 100

⇒ r = (302.5 / 3025) × 100 = **10%**

⇒ Now, for A₂: 3025 = P(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ 3025 = P(11/10)²

⇒ 3025 = P × (121/100)

⇒ P = (3025 × 100) / 121

⇒ P = 25 × 100 = **Rs. 2,500**

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,500 and 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Definition

Interest calculated on the initial **principal** and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Successive Amounts Ratio

The ratio of amounts in successive years is constant: Aₙ₊₁ / Aₙ = (1 + r/100).

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years: Difference = P(r/100)² | For 3 years: Difference = P(r/100)² × (3 + r/100).

questions.question: Ravi travels from City A to City B and from City B to City A in 4 hours. If the average speed of the total journey is 68.3 km/h, what is the distance between City A and City B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** is defined as **Total Distance** divided by **Total Time**.

Total Distance (A to B + B to A) = **Average Speed** × **Total Time**

⇒ Total Distance = 68.3 × 4 = 273.2 km

Since the distance between A and B is exactly half of the round-trip distance:

Distance AB = 273.2 ÷ 2 = 136.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 136.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Average Speed** of the journey = 68.3 km/h

**Total Time** taken for the round trip = 4 hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48e721136b618b71fb6fdcb294c6c95ca1953285c8cec7cdf516c57bcffd023c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Distance = Average Speed × Total Time

Distance (A to B) = Total Distance ÷ 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered by Ravi = 68.3 × 4

⇒ Total distance = 273.2 km

⇒ Let the distance between City A and City B be 'd'.

⇒ Total Distance = Distance(A→B) + Distance(B→A) = d + d = 2d

⇒ 2d = 273.2

⇒ d = 273.2 ÷ 2

⇒ d = 136.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 136.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time). It is not the simple arithmetic mean of speeds unless times are equal.

Harmonic Mean for Equal Distances

If a person travels equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed = (2 × v₁ × v₂) ÷ (v₁ + v₂).

Basic Relation

Distance = Speed × Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed.</p

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 17 ∶ 25 ∶ 66 and their HCF is 18. The smallest number among them is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 17 : 25 : 66

Highest Common Factor (HCF) = 18

Smallest number corresponds to the smallest ratio part (17).

Smallest number = Smallest ratio part × HCF

Smallest number = 17 × 18 = 306

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of three numbers = 17 : 25 : 66

HCF of the numbers = 18

**Formula Used:**

Actual Number = Ratio Part × HCF

 
 1st Number (17x)
 
 
 2nd Number (25x)
 
 
 3rd Number (66x)
 
 Common Factor (x) = HCF = 18
 Ratio Visualization

Let the three numbers be 17x, 25x, and 66x.

Since HCF is the greatest common divisor for all the numbers, x represents the HCF.

⇒ x = 18

⇒ First number = 17 × 18 = 306

⇒ Second number = 25 × 18 = 450

⇒ Third number = 66 × 18 = 1188

⇒ Comparing 306, 450, and 1188, the smallest number is 306.

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and Numbers in Ratio

If numbers are in ratio a : b : c and their HCF is h, then the numbers are ah, bh, and ch.

LCM of Numbers in Ratio

LCM of numbers having ratio a : b : c and HCF h is calculated as LCM(a, b, c) × h.

HCF × LCM Property

For two numbers A and B, A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B). Note: This is not directly applicable to more than two numbers.</p

Now, the number of days between 12 July 1966 to 14 August 1966:

= 19 (remaining days of July) + 14 (August) = 33 days.

= 33 days → 33/7 = 4 weeks and 5 odd days.

So, **14 August 1966** will be Tuesday + 5 = Sunday.

Hence, the correct answer is "Sunday".

questions.question: The length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 13 cm and the length of one of the other two sides is 5 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the triangle?

Recognize the **Pythagorean triplet**: **5, 12, 13**.

Given **hypotenuse = 13 cm** and **one side = 5 cm**, the **other side (height) must be 12 cm**.

Area = (1 ÷ 2) × base × height = (1 ÷ 2) × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ p² = 13² − 5²

⇒ p² = 169 − 25 = 144

⇒ p = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 5 × 12

⇒ Area = 5 × 6 = 30 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

Pythagorean Triplets

Common sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25).

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s = (a+b+c) ÷ 2.

questions.question: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC and ∠*BAC* = 50°. Side BC is extended to D. Find the measure of ∠*ACD*.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle** with **AB = AC**, base angles ∠ABC and ∠ACB are equal.

Base angles = (180° − 50°) ÷ 2 = 65°.

The **exterior angle** ∠ACD is equal to the sum of the two opposite **interior angles**.

∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 50° + 65° = 115°.

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB = AC** and ∠BAC = 50° in **▵ABC**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a **triangle** is 180°; **Linear pair** sum is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2842ee79687b82aa3f9f3b6cf70788dfd57b08f9b6b0d5f62a4fc064b3c9db1.png] 

In **▵ABC**, since **AB = AC**:

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 50° + 2 × ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠ACB = 180° − 50° = 130°

⇒ ∠ACB = 65°

Side **BC** is extended to **D**, forming a **linear pair** at point **C**:

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ 65° + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − 65° = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles of the triangle.

Isosceles Triangle Property

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.</p

• If worldwide salt consumption were reduced to the recommended amount then it is predicted that **2.5 million fatalities may be avoided annually**.
 
• According to WHO, **the maximum recommended salt consumption for adults should be reduced for children between the ages of two to fifteen based on their proportional energy needs to those of adults**.
 
• Around** 75% of the salt consumed** daily in many high-income nations **comes from processed foods and meals** served outside the home.

questions.question: A solid metallic cylindrical rod of radius 1.4 cm and length 24 cm is melted and recast as identical spherical balls of radius 2 mm. How many maximum such balls could be made?

⇒ a = 3 × H(R)²/4(r)3

⇒ a = 3 × 30 × 49 = 4410

**∴ Total no. of balls melted from the cylinder is 4410.**

questions.question: The Second Five-Year Plan was aimed at laying emphasis on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**industrial sector**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**

 
 
• The **second five-year plan gave industries**, mainly heavy industries a lot of attention.
 
• In contrast to the First Five Year Plan, which focused mostly on agriculture, the Second Plan encouraged **domestic industrial product production, especially in the growth of the public sector**.
 
• The strategy was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, an economic growth framework created in **1953** by** Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
• The strategy sought to identify the best distribution of investments among productive industries in order to **maximise long-term economic growth**.
 
• It made use of **cutting-edge operations research and optimization approaches** as well as creative uses of **statistical models created by the Indian Statistical Institute**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under the Second Five-Year Plan, the state focused on **consumer goods**, while the first plan's factories helped **boost overall industrial output**.
 
• With assistance from the Soviet Union, Britain (U.K.), and West Germany, hydroelectric power projects and five steel plants were built in **Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela, respectively**.
 
• Production of **coal** increased.
 
• In the northeast, more **railway lines were constructed**.
 
• In total, **48 billion rupees** were allotted for the Second Five-Year Plan in India.
 
• The following sectors received this sum: c**ommunications and transportation, miscellaneous, social services, power and irrigation, and other**.
 
• **Actual growth was** **4.27 per cent **compared to the **target growth rate of 4.5 per cent**.

questions.question: The Mohan Veena, a modified Hawaiian Guitar also known as Hindustani Slide Guitar was created and popularized by __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishwa Mohan Bhatt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohan Veena**

 
 
• A **Mohan Veena is one of two unique plucked string instruments used in Hindustani classical music**, a genre of Indian classical music associated with the country's north.
 
• First, in 1**948, Pandit Radhika Mohan Maitra** created a musical instrument that combined the sarod, the veena, and the surbahar.
 
• In **1949, Thakur Jaidev Singh**, the head producer of All India Radio at the time, gave the instrument the name **"Mohan veena" in honour of Pt. Maitra**.
 
• The **Grammy Award-winning Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt invented and popularised the Mohan Veena**, a Hawaiian guitar that has been modified.
 
• It is employed to perform** classical Hindustani Ragas**.
 
• **Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Salil Bhatt **(who later created the Satvik Veena, a variation of his father's Mohan Veena),** and Canadian blues singer Harry Manx** are a few of the well-known performers
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This instrument, which has **20 strings in total**, is actually a modified Archtop guitar.
 
• It has **three to four melody strings, four to five drone strings **strung from the peghead,** and twelve sympathetic strings **strung to tuners positioned on the side of the neck.
 
• To increase the sustain and resonance of the sound, a **gourd (or Tumba)** is put into the back of the neck.
 
• It is played with a **bar and held in the lap** similarly to a **slide guitar**.
 
• It is pulled by more than **500 pounds** of strings together, which is a lot of tension. 
 
• The **Chaturangui Veena, Hansa Veena, Shankar Veena**, and many other famous variations of the Mohan Veena exist in India.
